property_summary: For any caller, contract.owner() returns the stored owner address (the deployer/owner), but the mutant returns msg.sender so for some caller addresses the returned value differs.

For any caller who is the current owner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) must revert (i.e., not succeed) when newOwner == address(0); the mutant removes this check and thus will succeed for newOwner == address(0).

For any caller that is the current owner and for any address candidate newOwner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) on the correct contract reverts if and only if newOwner == address(0); the mutant removes the require and thus allows transfer to address(0) (i.e. for some newOwner the call succeeds on the mutant but should revert on the reference).

For any caller who is the current owner and any address candidate newOwner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) on the correct contract always reverts if newOwner == address(0) (owner cannot be set to zero); the mutant removes that check so there exist inputs (newOwner == address(0)) where transferOwnership succeeds on the mutant but must revert on the reference.

For any caller who is the current owner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) on the reference contract always succeeds (returns/does not revert) and updates owner to newOwner; the mutant erroneates by reverting unless newOwner equals the current owner, so there exist inputs (current owner calling with a different newOwner) where the mutant reverts while the reference succeeds.

For any caller who is the current owner and any target newOwner address, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) on the correct contract succeeds (does not revert) and sets owner to newOwner; the mutant adds a require that newOwner == owner(), causing calls that attempt to change owner to a different address to revert (breaking that rule).

Invariant: only the externally owned account that is the current owner (owner() == msg.sender) can successfully call transferOwnership; the mutant that checks tx.origin instead of msg.sender allows a contract caller (via a forwarding contract) to bypass owner restriction and thus can make transferOwnership succeed when the direct msg.sender would not be owner, violating the invariant for some caller addresses.

For any caller address X and any target newOwner Y, only a direct call where msg.sender == owner() can successfully transfer ownership in the reference contract; the mutant that checks tx.origin instead of msg.sender allows a contract to forward a call (so tx.origin == owner but msg.sender != owner) to succeed, so there exist caller/target pairs where transferOwnership succeeds on the mutant but would be rejected by the reference.

For any caller and newOwner the reference contract only allows transferOwnership when msg.sender == owner(), so a forwarded call through a contract (where tx.origin == owner but msg.sender != owner) must revert on the reference but can succeed on the mutant that compares tx.origin; the test fuzzes an owner EOA and a forwarding contract caller to show mutant accepts a forwarded transfer while reference rejects it.

For all callers, only a direct call from the owner (msg.sender == owner()) can successfully call transferOwnership on the correct contract; the mutant that checks tx.origin instead of msg.sender allows a forwarded call (msg.sender != owner but tx.origin == owner) to succeed, violating this rule for some forwarded-call inputs.

For all callers, the reference contract only allows transferOwnership when the immediate msg.sender is the owner; the mutant that uses tx.origin instead can be tricked by a forwarding contract so a call that the reference would revert (msg.sender != owner) can succeed on the mutant (tx.origin == owner).

Only the caller passed as _distributor to setRewardDistributor can become rewardDistributor (i.e., rewardDistributor equals the function argument), so rewardDistributor == _distributor after the call.

Only the externally supplied caller (msg.sender) can become the rewardDistributor after setRewardDistributor is called (i.e., rewardDistributor equals tx.origin only if tx.origin == msg.sender, otherwise it equals the provided _distributor).
